author: Yelena Mandenberg
title: Chilling 911 call behind missing Alabama family facing deportation - NewsBreak
text:
By Yelena Mandenberg ,
4 hours ago
A 911 call from a worried neighbor is providing fresh insight into the mysterious disappearance of a woman and her two children in Alabama.
Aurelia Choc Cac, 40, along with her daughter Niurka Zuleta Choc, 17, and toddler son Anthony Garcia Choc, were last seen at their home in Mobile County, Alabama, on Friday, January 30, at 3 pm before they went missing. According to call records obtained by FOX10, Maurice Smith told emergency operators that Cac had a "crazy ex-boyfriend," who he claims has been on the run for at least eight months.
The neighbor is identified as Maurice Simmons in an NBC 15 report. He mentioned he'd chatted with Cac, who hails from Guatemala, on Friday evening and she gave no hint she was planning to go anywhere.
The 40-year-old mother and her two children have mysteriously disappeared from their Alabama residence, with local authorities suggesting foul play could be a factor.
The Mobile County Sheriff's Office has pointed to "signs of a struggle" at their property and believes the three were "taken against their will," according to a weekend press release.
The family was last spotted on Friday, with police responding to a report about a "suspicious disappearance" on Saturday, at which time they officially declared the family missing. "We do believe the mother, daughter, and son were taken against their will, and we believe they could be in danger," stated the sheriff's office, as reported by Mirror US.
The mother was last seen wearing a maroon jacket and tan pants, standing about 5 feet tall and weighing approximately 140 pounds.
Her 17-year-old daughter, Niurka, was dressed in a black top and plaid pants, stands at 5'1" and weighs about 100 pounds. Two-year-old Anthony, with his dark hair, was last seen in a sweatshirt adorned with a cartoon character and blue jeans.
DON'T MISS...
Anthony Garcia Choc, and 17-year old Niurka Zuleta Choc, are still missing Sheriff Paul Burch revealed that responding officers discovered blood scattered throughout the house and cash left behind, as per NBC 15. "There was obviously some kind of struggle, based on the scene," he said, according to FOX 10. Burch noted that there were "clothes throughout the bedroom that appeared to be dumped out and hampers missing. "
He also mentioned a missing mattress with a box spring, indicating it wasn't very old, which he described as "unusual," as reported by NBC 15. Burch disclosed that Aurelia and her 17-year-old daughter, a junior at Theodore High School, had final deportation orders issued last April. The two-year-old boy is a U.S. citizen.
In their initial statement, the sheriff's office indicated they were investigating a person of interest, a 30-year-old male who is "known" to Cac.
However, after interviewing this individual, the sheriff's office clarified that he is not considered a suspect. Local police have been following up on multiple leads and are appealing for anyone with information to come forward. The family of three has now been missing for five days.
While authorities have received a number of tips, they haven't revealed the details of these leads. Statistics show that if someone goes missing for more than a week, the chances of locating them drop considerably. Although more than 90% of cases are solved within a month, the initial 48 to 72 hours are critical in finding a missing person, with leads typically becoming scarce after this period, making the search increasingly difficult.
Through a translator, Aurelia's eldest daughter, Lorena, made an emotional appeal for information about her family's disappearance. "Whoever did this, please bring my little brother home," said Lorena. "I'm waiting for them to come home with the little baby."
Anyone with information is being urged to contact them at 251-574-8633.
